comparisons.peer_topic: Credit Risk Management Policies for Investments
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company limits credit risk by placing investments with high credit quality financial institutions, requiring commercial paper to be rated A1/P1/F1 or better and bonds to be rated A/A2 or better.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD explicitly state a policy of placing investments with high-credit-quality financial institutions to manage credit risk. Intel limits exposure based on the counterparty's credit standing and requires investment-grade debt instruments, while AMD specifies minimum rating thresholds for commercial paper (A1, P1, F1) and bonds (A, A2) and requires collateral for repurchase agreements. Both adopt a conservative approach to counterparty selection, though AMD provides more granular rating criteria in the text.

sentences.text: We generally place investments with high-credit-quality counterparties and, by policy, we limit the amount of credit exposure to any one counterparty based on our analysis of that counterparty's relative credit standing.
As required per our investment policy, substantially all of our investments in debt instruments are in investment-grade instruments.
The Company places its investments with high credit quality financial institutions.
At the time an investment is made, investments in commercial paper of industrial firms and financial institutions are rated A1, P1, F1 or better.
The Company invests in bonds that are rated A, A2 or better and repurchase agreements, each of which have securities of the type and quality listed above as collateral.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company mitigates credit risks on cash and accounts receivable by using high-quality financial institutions, spreading risks across multiple counterparties, performing regular credit evaluations, and requiring collateral in certain circumstances.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom (AVGO) both address credit risk concentrations and the mitigation strategy involving high-quality counterparties. Intel states it generally places investments with high-credit-quality counterparties and limits exposure based on credit standing analysis. Similarly, Broadcom maintains cash with high-credit-quality financial institutions and seeks to mitigate credit risks by spreading risks across multiple counterparties and monitoring their risk profiles. Both companies focus on institutional counterparty quality and diversification/spreading of risk to mitigate exposure.

comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron (MU) share similar language regarding the management of credit risk concentrations. Both identify cash, derivatives, and receivables as instruments subject to credit risk and state that they invest with high-credit-quality institutions. Both companies also explicitly state a policy to limit credit exposure/concentration by restricting investments with any single obligor and monitoring counterparties. Intel additionally notes that substantially all debt investments are investment-grade, while MU emphasizes limiting exposure per single obligor.

comparisons.peer_topic: Concentration of Credit Risk and Financial Instruments
comparisons.peer_summary: The company is subject to credit risk primarily through cash equivalents, marketable securities, and accounts receivable. To manage this risk, the company maintains a policy of investing in highly-rated fixed income securities with diversified exposures and duration limits, while performing ongoing credit evaluations of customers and maintaining an allowance for potential credit losses.
comparisons.comparison: Intel, AMD, Micron, and NVIDIA all disclose policies for managing credit risk associated with financial instruments such as cash, securities, and receivables. A key similarity is the emphasis on counterparty quality: Intel requires high-credit-quality counterparties and investment-grade instruments; AMD specifies A/P/F1 and A/A2 ratings; Micron uses high-credit-quality institutions and limits single-obligor exposure; and NVIDIA requires highly-rated fixed income securities and diversification. All four companies focus on mitigating risk through strict investment policies and counterparty selection, though the specific mechanisms (e.g., NVIDIA's mention of diversification and duration limits, AMD's explicit rating codes) vary.
